reader.notes: ModScaled computes the truncating quotient and subtracts one when the signs differ and the remainder is nonzero (the floor), so every RV2 row and every probed boundary matches the RV1 formula. The 1985 citation form §1985:A.2.28.4 fails cite.py (no-clause); Section A is cited with the amendment token §1989. The seed site NumericRenderer.cs#Power is not on MOD's path.

refuter.evidence: q5mod.cob at --std 85 (runs/q5mod-001): COMP -11 with SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE -5 -> -1; COMP -11, unsigned 5 -> 4; COMP-3 11, -5 -> -4; COMP-3 11, 5 -> 1; MOD(MOD(-11 5) -3) -> -2; MOD(INTEGER(-2.5) 5) -> 2; MOD(-B3 + 0, -U1) -> -1; MOD(-11 -5) into PIC 9 -> 1; MOD(-11 5)*10 + MOD(11 -5) -> 36; MOD(-1 5) -> 4, MOD(-5 5) -> 0, MOD(4 -5) -> -1: every value is RV1's floored formula and the four RV2 rows hold for every usage tried. q6modbad.cob: MOD(FUNCTION NUMVAL("11") 5) refused COBOL1627 (numeric function where integer required, as §1989:A.2.3 numeric functions bar). Side note, not this rule: q7modexp.cob MOD(-11 / 1, 5) is admitted and returns 4 although §1989:A.2.2 AR4 asks for an expression 'which will always result in an integer value' (an AR-rule question for the argument rule's reader). cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.28.4 RV2  (2.28.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV2'; 'OK  §1989:A.2.28.4 RV1  ... the text is in RV1'; 'OK  §1989:A.2.2 ... it lies in AR4'.
